description: Pairing-code normalization. The server is the truth: reject input that is empty or longer than max_input_length characters; upper-case the whole string (locale-independent); drop every character in server_strip; fold I and L to 1 and O to 0; any other character outside the alphabet makes the input not a code (U included); exactly symbol_count symbols must remain. 'normalized' is the canonical ungrouped code and 'grouped' the XXXX-XXXX-XXXX display form, both null when the input is not a code. A client must produce exactly these values, with ONE permitted leniency: a case marked client_may_accept differs from a valid code only by carriage returns and line feeds (client_extra_strip), and a client may either refuse it like the server (null) or accept it as exactly client_normalized / client_grouped. That leniency is harmless only because a client that applies it sends the server the normalized code, never the raw input; a client that forwards raw typed input must not use it to decide anything the server would decide differently.

cases.name: canonical
cases.why: Already canonical: returned unchanged.

cases.name: grouped-dashes
cases.why: The display form the desktop shows.

cases.name: lowercase
cases.why: Typed in lowercase: upper-cased before anything else.

cases.name: mixed-case
cases.why: Mixed case.

cases.name: grouped-spaces
cases.why: Spaces are stripped like dashes.

cases.name: grouped-tabs
cases.why: Tabs are in the server's strip set too.

cases.name: surrounding-spaces
cases.why: Leading and trailing spaces are stripped.

cases.name: irregular-separators
cases.why: Separators anywhere, repeated: grouping is not checked.

cases.name: all-digits
cases.why: Digits only.

cases.name: fold-i-l-o
cases.why: I and L fold to 1, O folds to 0.

cases.name: fold-lowercase
cases.why: Folding happens after upper-casing, so i, l and o fold too.

cases.name: illegal-u
cases.why: U is not folded: it is simply not a symbol.

cases.name: illegal-lowercase-u
cases.why: Nor is u.

cases.name: illegal-punctuation
cases.why: Only dash, space and tab are separators.

cases.name: illegal-underscore
cases.why: Underscore is not a separator.

cases.name: too-short
cases.why: 11 symbols.

cases.name: too-long
cases.why: 13 symbols.

cases.name: empty
cases.why: Empty is not a code.

cases.name: only-separators
cases.why: Zero symbols.

cases.name: max-input-length-64
cases.why: Exactly 64 characters including padding: still accepted.

cases.name: overlong-input-65
cases.why: 65 characters: refused before normalizing, even though the symbols inside are a valid code. The bound is on raw input length.

cases.name: overlong-input-garbage
cases.why: Far over the bound.

cases.name: fullwidth-letters
cases.why: Fullwidth Latin lookalikes are not the ASCII symbols.

cases.name: fullwidth-digits
cases.why: Fullwidth digits are not digits here either.

cases.name: cyrillic-lookalike
cases.why: Cyrillic capital A looks like A and is not.

cases.name: kelvin-sign
cases.why: KELVIN SIGN upper-cases to itself, not to K.

cases.name: zero-width-space
cases.why: Zero-width space is not in the strip set.

cases.name: no-break-space
cases.why: NO-BREAK SPACE is not an ASCII space.

cases.name: combining-accent
cases.why: A combining mark makes the last symbol not a symbol.

cases.name: emoji
cases.why: Astral-plane characters are refused.

cases.name: dotted-capital-i
cases.why: Turkish dotted capital I upper-cases to itself: refused.

cases.name: dotless-small-i
cases.why: Turkish dotless small i upper-cases to plain I, which then folds to 1. Locale-independent upper-casing is part of the rule.

cases.name: sharp-s-expands
cases.why: German sharp s upper-cases to SS: one input character becomes two symbols. Upper-case the whole string first, then iterate.

cases.name: ligature-ff-expands
cases.why: The ff ligature upper-cases to FF, also two symbols.

cases.name: trailing-newline
cases.why: A pasted code with a trailing newline.

cases.name: trailing-crlf
cases.why: A pasted code with a Windows line ending.

cases.name: embedded-newlines
cases.why: Groups on separate lines.

cases.name: embedded-cr
cases.why: Bare carriage returns between groups.

cases.name: newline-does-not-rescue-illegal
cases.why: Stripping newlines never makes an illegal symbol legal.

cases.name: newline-does-not-rescue-length
cases.why: Nor a wrong length.
